headword: {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}
gloss: the Day of the Ox in midsummer (eel day)

definitions.gloss: the Day of the Ox in midsummer
definitions.explanation: A day of the ox (in the old twelve-day cycle) that falls during the summer {土用|どよう}, the eighteen days before the start of autumn, usually in late July. Eating eel ({鰻|うなぎ}) on this day to beat the summer heat is a firm custom.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}だ。
examples.english: Today is the Day of the Ox.

examples.japanese: {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{鰻|うなぎ}→鰻：06105_unagi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate eel on the Day of the Ox.

examples.japanese: {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}づく→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦スーパー→スーパー：01061_suupaa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鰻|うなぎ}→鰻：06105_unagi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{蒲焼|かばや}き→蒲焼き：29221_kabayaki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: As the Day of the Ox approaches, supermarkets fill up with grilled eel.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The custom is popularly credited to the Edo-period scholar {平賀源内|ひらがげんない}, who is said to have helped an eel shop sell more in summer; the story is a legend, but the custom is real. Some years have two such days (⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丑|うし} and ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丑|うし}). Eel is said to give stamina against ⟦{夏|なつ}バテ→夏バテ：15545_natsubate⟧.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{土用|どよう}→土用：27533_doyou⟧: the seasonal period before each change of season
- ⟦{鰻|うなぎ}→鰻：06105_unagi⟧: eel
- ⟦{夏|なつ}バテ→夏バテ：15545_natsubate⟧: summer fatigue
